quotes.text: You can't protect what you can't see. If your security data is scattered across 20 dashboards, you're blind.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Captures the core argument for centralizing security logs.

quotes.text: By the time you stumble to your laptop and log in, the attack has already done what they came to do. Automation isn't a luxury. It's a necessity.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Makes the case for automated incident response in plain terms.

quotes.text: Attackers think in graphs, not lists. They don't see individual users and devices, they see the connections between them.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Explains why graph-based investigation matters for defenders.

quotes.text: The data lake removes the trade off between cost and visibility so you no longer have to decide between keeping logs and saving money. You can do both.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Summarizes the economic shift of long-term log retention.

quotes.text: The hardest part isn't the technology. It's knowing where to begin. So here's my advice. Start with one data source and one detection rule.
quotes.speaker: Mirko Peters
quotes.why: Gives a concrete, low-barrier starting recommendation.

takeaways: Microsoft Sentinel combines SIEM correlation and SOAR automation so signals from Entra, Exchange, SharePoint and Defender become one story instead of scattered alerts.
The Sentinel data lake separates cheap storage from compute, making multi-year log retention affordable and enabling hunting for low-and-slow attacks.
Start small: enable Sentinel in the Defender portal, connect Entra ID sign-in logs and install one detection rule from the content hub.
hook: Security signals in Microsoft 365 are scattered across Entra, Exchange, SharePoint and Defender, so slow attacks slip through unnoticed. This episode explains Microsoft Sentinel in plain English for Microsoft 365 admins, from SIEM and SOAR to the new data lake, graphs and AI. You will learn how to get started with one connector and one detection rule without a big security budget.
